title: Anybody in the public has access to buy your company
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Do you know what actually happens when a company goes public?
A student asked: do you have to be a publicly traded company to be on the stock market? Jose said: yes. There are reporting requirements and minimum revenues.
Another asked: is the benefit of going public so you can create that market cap for yourself? Jose said: yes. What it does is give you access to capital, because anybody can buy your stock.

Jose said that, when you buy a stock, there are systems with reporting requirements, and a digital ledger tells you how much stock you bought, at what price and at what time. As people buy a stock that is performing well, more people can buy it, and anybody around the world can access it.

groups.heading: Anybody in the public has access to buy your company

lines.text: If you are a private company, Jose said, you don't have that kind of access. You are going person to person or business to business. That is a totally different game. Here, somebody you don't know at all has access to buy your company stock.

Before you go public, he said, investment banks do the underwriting. They do the paperwork, present the company and fix the price you go public at. All of this is heavily regulated by the securities regulator, because in the old days somebody could just take off with the money. Now you can look at the balance sheet of a company, so you know what you are buying.

He gave an example of a company whose stock rose while it was losing millions of dollars a year. People investing weren't checking that. They said: this is a great company, they're all over the world. Jose said that a friend of his who runs hotels does the math in his head: how many beds, what is the turnover, what is the occupancy rate. Looking at the fundamentals, he said there is no way it works.
Which fundamentals could you work out in your head about your own business?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write whether a company like yours could go public, and what it would need.
Write the reporting you would have to do.
Write the three fundamentals you can work out in your head for your own business.
Write what you would check before buying any stock.
Write who could teach you to read a balance sheet.

check.q: What did Jose say going public gives a company?
What did Jose say investment banks do before a company goes public?
choices: The underwriting: the paperwork, the presentation and the price

check.q: What fundamentals did Jose's friend work out in his head for hotels?

recap: Know how a public company works, and check the fundamentals.
